subject: AWS marketplace: unexplained usage adjustments & VAT breakdown — ACME Corp
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Lauren Morris <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS marketplace: unexplained usage adjustments & VAT breakdown — ACME Corp

Hi Lauren / Priya,

Following up on last week's batch close: ACME flagged two items on their June 1 marketplace invoice that we can't reconcile on our side. The key points:

- There is a $12,300 negative adjustment listed under "Usage corrections" for merchant ID M-89321 that doesn't appear in our daily metering exports (we attach our May 31 export below).
- VAT treatment: the invoice shows a 20% VAT pass-through on a subset of lines but the ledger attribution is split between our EU entity and our US SaaS entity — ACME needs a clear VAT breakdown per line so they can reclaim.

Can AWS confirm the source of the usage correction (refund vs. duplicate meter ingestion), provide a per-line VAT flag, and confirm which seller entity was billed? We need this before we release the related payout.

I've attached our metering_report_acme_20260531.csv and the draft invoice we generated for cross-checking. If you need any additional IDs (listing IDs, order IDs, marketplace SKU), tell me which ones and I will surface them.

Goal: get a line-level reconciliation and a short note we can share with ACME finance so they can process payment or dispute correctly.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference
From: Lauren Morris <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: aws-payments-ops@amazon.com, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS marketplace: unexplained usage adjustments & VAT breakdown — ACME Corp

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the details and the export. I've pulled the marketplace logs and the short answer: the $12,300 negative adjustment is a result of a duplicate-metering dedup pass that ran during the May 28 ingest window. The root cause was a retry loop from a third-party connector for listing L-448 that caused two meter events to land for the same usage IDs.

What I can provide today:
- A corrected invoice (see attached invoice_20260601_ACME.pdf) with the duplicate lines removed and an explanation block.
- A per-line VAT flag file (we can provide CSV) and confirmation that the billed entity was "Redwood Inference LLC (US)" for the affected lines; the EU VAT pass-through applied to lines where ACME's EU tenant ID was used at purchase time.
- Evidence: transaction IDs and ingest fingerprints for the dedup (we can export as redwood-evidence-bundle.zip).

Next steps I propose:
1) I will upload the corrected invoice to the seller console and send you the finalized PDF (attached).
2) Please confirm whether Redwood will accept the corrected invoice as the invoice of record so we can release the merchant payout.
3) If ACME needs an entity-level VAT breakdown for reprovisioning or reclaim, let us know the exact format (per-line vs aggregated by entity).

I attached the corrected invoice and a small evidence bundle. If you want the raw ingest logs I can work with payments ops to produce them (they might need a day).

Best,
Lauren Morris
AWS Marketplace Payments – Partner Ops
aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: AWS marketplace: unexplained usage adjustments & VAT breakdown — ACME Corp

Marissa / Monica — forwarding Lauren's response. Short summary and ask:

- Cause: duplicate-metering dedup during May 28 ingest (AWS confirms).
- Deliverables from AWS: corrected invoice, per-line VAT flags, ingest fingerprints (evidence bundle).
- Impact: $12.3k negative adjustment reduces ACME's payable amount; AWS is asking if Redwood will accept corrected invoice as invoice of record to release payout.

Action items for Redwood:
1) Marissa — confirm whether we accept the corrected invoice and sign off for payout release. If we need AWS to reassign any lines to our EU entity for VAT clarity, enumerate those specific lines.
2) Monica — if we accept the corrected invoice, do we hold payout until ACME confirms payment? We may need to coordinate a short hold and produce the VAT per-entity breakdown to ACME so they can reclaim VAT.
3) Karthik — liaison with ACME if they need a formal statement for tax reclaim.

Priya — looping ACME so you see AWS's note. Let us know whether ACME prefers per-line VAT flags or a summarized VAT-by-entity spreadsheet to feed to your tax team.

Jonas

On Jun 10, 2026, Lauren Morris <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com> wrote:
> Hi Jonas,
> 
> Thanks for the details and the export. I've pulled the marketplace logs...
> (see attached invoice_20260601_ACME.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AWS marketplace: unexplained usage adjustments & VAT breakdown — ACME Corp

Thanks for the summary, Jonas. Quick checklist from Marketplace Billing:

- I agree we should accept the corrected invoice as invoice of record so the merchant payout can proceed. AWS's explanation is reasonable and they attached the evidence bundle.
- Please request AWS to: (a) produce a per-line VAT flag CSV keyed by marketplace SKU + order id, (b) include the seller entity column (US vs EU) for each line. That will let us map the VAT to our ledgers.
- We'll prepare a short reconciliation memo (1 page) to send to ACME finance that includes: original invoice line, corrected invoice line, adjustment reason, and VAT entity.

I've attached a draft memo template to this thread (redwood-evidence-bundle.zip includes the template). Karthik: can you pick up the outreach to ACME tax contact if Priya asks for additional documentation?

Marissa Cole
Marketplace Billing Lead
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-corp.com>, Lauren Morris <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AWS marketplace: unexplained usage adjustments & VAT breakdown — ACME Corp

Hi all,

I reviewed the corrected invoice and the evidence Lauren attached. Finance will accept AWS's corrected invoice as invoice of record under the following conditions:

1) AWS confirms the per-line seller entity column and provides the VAT flags in CSV format (we prefer SKU, order_id, line_amount, vat_rate, seller_entity).
2) ACME confirms whether they will process the corrected amount or raise a formal dispute by EOD June 15. If ACME disputes, hold payout until dispute resolution.
3) Please include the PO number in AWS's evidence bundle or the corrected PDF (ACME PO #ACME-9876).

Assuming conditions above are met, Redwood Finance authorizes release of the merchant payout for the reconciled invoice. We'll also attach our 1-page reconciliation memo when we notify ACME.

Jonas/Marissa: if Lauren can push the CSV and add the PO number in the portal, we'll mark this resolved on our side and notify ACME to proceed with payment processing.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Manager, Financial Operations
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference
